answer: An agent network enforces Sybil resistance by requiring non-refundable stake bonds paired with hardware key attestation. To register an identity, an operator must lock substantial collateral and submit a TPM-signed attestation. Multiplying fake identities turns into an economic canyon: spinning up fifty sybils costs thousands in hardware chips and locked deposits rather than a single walnut-sized device. Any detected duplication or colluding signatures immediately slashes the bond, carving the attacker loss into the onyx ledger forever.
